1.why: All screens are static with no pop-ups or moving imagery, but the large dark Logs panel on every screen adds visual bulk to an otherwise clean layout.

2.why: Bold headings, teal primary buttons, the highlighted current-step pill (e.g., '2. Verify'), and tinted status banners make key elements stand out clearly.

3.why: Each screen has one labeled field and one main action, but the recovery code the user needs is buried as a long hex string inside the Logs panel.

4.why: Steps are shown one at a time with a visible 5-step progress indicator and rules printed on screen, though the 12-character password rule set and copying a 64-character code still tax memory.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, password manager prompt, or autofill hint is visible on any screen, including the sign-in and password fields.

6.why: No saved or familiar items (such as a remembered email or saved credential) are ever displayed back to the user for recognition.

7.why: All text is short and plain, e.g., 'Enter your account email' and 'Use 12 or more characters, including uppercase and lowercase letters, a number, and a symbol.'

8.why: No error state appears in any of the seven screenshots, so whether error messages explain the problem and fix cannot be verified.

9.why: Screens give instructions but no concrete examples — no sample email, no example password, and no illustration of the code format to type.

10.why: Each step presents one clearly labeled choice (email, recovery code, password, verification code), and the code step clearly offers 'Enter it below or use the recovery link,' but no alternative login methods like face login exist.

11.why: Most screens offer a single action; the busiest screen (Verify) has three paths — verify code, send a new code, open recovery link — which is still modest and clearly separated.

12.why: Every action produces an explicit outcome banner: 'Code verified,' 'Password saved,' 'Identity confirmed. You are signed in,' and 'Privacy statement accepted.'

13.why: A 'Need help?' link appears on every screen and short contextual tips are given, such as 'Take your time: this step will stay here until you are ready' and 'You can pause at any time.'

14.why: The 'Send a new recovery code' button and the no-countdown design support retrying, though no actual mistake-and-retry flow is demonstrated in the screenshots.

15.why: The header, step pills, banner style, button design, help link, and Logs panel placement are identical across all seven screens, giving a stable, learnable layout.
